## What it is

Kolibri is an **offline learning platform** from Learning Equality: courses, videos, exercises and quizzes, with classes, learner progress and coach reports. It works with no internet once content is imported ([learningequality/kolibri](https://github.com/learningequality/kolibri)). It is the courses part of the **Offline Knowledge** bundle (REC-NOMAD-01) and fits the Family stream's kids' learning (docs/APPS.md).

**Licence:** `MIT` ([LICENSE at v0.19.5](https://github.com/learningequality/kolibri/blob/f7cafd40f5c339b0ffadc36aa8de10ea79a9175b/LICENSE)), Market class **L1** (license-matrix row "Kolibri" [C-LIC-054]). **Channels carry their own licences, per resource.** Some are non-commercial (row "Content: Kolibri Studio channels"), so OneMind ships Kolibri with no channel imported.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`) from the official image `ghcr.io/learningequality/kolibri` (docker/README.md), as the image's `kolibri` user (UID 1000). No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Upstream's entrypoint starts as root, chowns the data and drops privileges with `setpriv`. Here the pod starts as UID 1000 directly. The command does the two remaining jobs itself: it keeps a stable Morango node id in `$KOLIBRI_HOME/.node_id` (used when syncing between Kolibri devices), then runs `kolibri start --foreground`.
- Ports: **8080** is the app. **8081** is Kolibri's separate "zip content" origin, which serves interactive content (HTML5 apps, H5P, exercises) sandboxed on its own port (docker/README.md "Ports"). Both are on the Service.
- `KOLIBRI_DISABLE_PING=true`: by default Kolibri sends usage statistics to Learning Equality's telemetry server (`kolibri/utils/options.py`, `Deployment.DISABLE_PING`). OneMind sends nothing unasked.
- Volume `kolibri-data` (32 GiB) at `/kolibri`: SQLite databases (users, classes, progress), settings and imported content. Backups run **cold** (the app is stopped while it is copied, which keeps SQLite consistent) and skip `content/`, which is imported again from Kolibri Studio.
- The first start migrates the databases, which takes a minute or more on a Pi. A startup probe allows up to 10 minutes.

## First run

Source: [Initial setup](https://kolibri.readthedocs.io/en/latest/install/initial_setup.html) and [Manage resources](https://kolibri.readthedocs.io/en/latest/manage/resources.html).

1. Install Kolibri from the Market (or with the Offline Knowledge bundle) and approve the action. It installs into `app-kolibri`.
2. Forward both ports and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-kolibri port-forward svc/kolibri 8080:8080 8081:8081
   ```
3. The setup wizard asks for the language, the kind of device (choose a group learning server for a household or classroom), a facility name and a super admin account. Do this straight after install: until then anyone who can reach the page can set it up.
4. Import content: **Device → Channels → Import**, from Kolibri Studio (needs internet once) or from a USB drive or another Kolibri on the network. Check the licence shown on each channel before importing it on a box you sell or share.

## Not done yet

- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: the app is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists. Interactive content needs both ports forwarded.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: Kolibri writes caches under its home and has not been tested with a read-only root.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices from idle use plus headroom for imports; they are checked against real use when the CI smoke test runs.

## Why this app is blocked

The licence and packaging are fine, but the pinned image fails the scan gate (contract §9.4 check 4). Trivy 0.76.2 (the gate's version) was run locally against `ghcr.io/learningequality/kolibri:0.19.5@sha256:19810f67…` on 2026-11-14, for amd64 and arm64. It found 5 CRITICAL findings that have a fixed version:

- `perl-base` (Debian 13 base): CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-42496, CVE-2026-8376 (fixed in 5.40.1-6+deb13u1);
- `Django`: CVE-2025-64459 (fixed in 5.2.8, 5.1.14, 4.2.26);
- `certifi`: GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 (fixed in 2026.10.18).

So the gate computes tier **blocked**: the Market lists Kolibri but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1), and the bundle installer skips it (it is optional there). The gate was not weakened. CI confirmed it: ci-apps run 43591778335, job `gate (kolibri)` (PR #124, 2026-11-14), computed tier `blocked` with the same 5 findings.

To unblock: 0.19.5 is the newest Kolibri release and image tag (registry read 2026-11-14), so there is nothing newer to pin. Kolibri unblocks when Learning Equality publishes an image rebuilt on a patched base with Django ≥ 5.2.8. The daily `apps-rescan` picks up a new tag once a PR bumps the pin. An upstream issue asking for a rebuild is the quickest path.
